concept_uz: Yangi sonlar kim qayerda turishini talashadi. Qirol tayogʻini yerga yotqizadi — sonlar oʻqi: katta son oʻngroqda. Paradda toq askarlar «juft-juft» saflana olmaydi, qirol esa oʻzini juft deb eʼlon qiladi: «Oʻzim bilan — nol qoʻshuv nol!»
style_line: Premium 3D animated feature film style, gentle split light — cool moonlight from the left, warm sunlight from the right — soft shadows, rich colours, vertical 9:16. No text, no captions, no letters or numerals written anywhere, no watermark.

refs.prompt: Vertical 9:16 full-body character portrait. A round king shaped like a thick, chunky upright ring with a small hole in the middle, so its wide front face is a disc. The ring is coloured like a yin-yang: the left half dark moon-silver with one small bright gold dot, the right half bright sun-gold with one small dark silver dot, the two halves curving into each other in a smooth S-shaped wave — made of polished metal, not a flat printed symbol. Big kind expressive eyes and a small mouth on the front of the ring, thin cartoon arms and legs, a small jewelled crown tilted to the left, holding a long plain wooden staff. He stands in the middle of a vast low-poly crystal plain, exactly where the cool left side meets the warm right side, front view, centred.

Vertical 9:16 full-body character portrait. A slim upright sun-gold character shaped like a tall narrow pillar with a small slanted flag-like tip at the top, big cheerful eyes, a wide smile, thin cartoon arms and legs, and a small round badge with a plus sign pinned on its chest. It stands on the vast low-poly crystal plain, front view, centred.

Change this character: exactly the same shape, size and face, but made of shining moon-silver instead of gold, eyebrows lowered in a grumpy frown, arms crossed, and a horizontal dark-blue sash wrapped across its middle instead of the plus badge. Same plain, same framing, full body, front view.

Vertical 9:16 wide landscape. A vast empty low-poly crystal plain made of smooth faceted triangular polygons: cool lavender-blue facets on the left, warm amber facets on the right, blending softly in the middle. A thin glowing straight path runs across the ground from left to right through the centre. The sky is split the same gentle way: soft twilight indigo with a few stars on the left, where a pale moon with a gentle old woman's face smiles; warm morning light on the right, where a big warm sun with a kind old grandfather's face — smiling eyes, bushy eyebrows and a beard of rays — smiles back. Not dark, just a gentle difference between the two sides. No characters.

Vertical 9:16. The king's long wooden staff lying flat on the low-poly crystal plain from left to right, with evenly spaced carved notches along it, the middle notch glowing gold. Low camera angle along the staff, morning light, no characters.

The ring-king stands at the glowing middle notch of the staff lying on the plain; many small number-characters stand one at each notch — silver ones on the left side of the picture (the cool moon side), gold ones on the right side (the warm sun side), in a neat row. Keep the king's design exactly the same. Vertical 9:16.

Change the scene to a parade: the same row of characters, every other one wearing a small blue cap and the ones between wearing small red caps, and in front of them a strict drill-sergeant character with a whistle. Vertical 9:16.

scenes.prompt: Chaos on the plain: dozens of gold and silver characters jostle, one climbs onto another's head, silver ones wander among gold ones. The silver character, squashed in the crowd, says in Uzbek with a slightly croaky, grumpy young boy's voice: "Kim qayerda turadi o'zi?!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

The ring-king raises his long staff angrily and the crowd cowers. He pauses, sighs, lowers it gently and says in Uzbek with a warm, slightly dramatic middle-aged male voice: "Yo'q… boshqacha qilaman." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

The staff lies on the ground and one by one carved notches glow along it. Off screen the king says in Uzbek with a warm, slightly dramatic middle-aged male voice: "Har bir chiziqcha — bitta sonning joyi. Kim katta bo'lsa, o'ngroqda turadi!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Har bir chiziqcha — bitta sonning joyi. Kim katta boʻlsa, oʻngroqda turadi!

scenes.prompt: The characters stand at their notches in perfect order. The silver character leans out and peers far to the left at a smaller silver character and says in Uzbek with a slightly croaky, grumpy young boy's voice: "Minus besh mendan kichik ekan — u chaproqda!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Minus besh mendan kichik ekan — u chaproqda!

scenes.prompt: The drill sergeant blows the whistle and says in Uzbek with a loud, strict army-sergeant man's voice: "Juft-juft safga turinglar!" The red-capped soldiers look at each other, confused. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

The red-capped soldiers throw up their hands and one of them says in Uzbek with a squeaky, cheeky young soldier's voice: "Bizda juft yo'q — biz toqmiz!" The parade collapses into a comic pile-up, caps flying. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

The ring-king steps forward proudly and says in Uzbek with a warm, slightly dramatic middle-aged male voice: "Men ham juftman!" A voice from the crowd says in Uzbek with a crowd of cheerful mixed voices: "Kim bilan?" The king grins and says in Uzbek with a warm, slightly dramatic middle-aged male voice: "O'zim bilan — nol qo'shuv nol!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

Back in line, every character is squeezed onto its tiny notch, elbows in each other's faces, and together they chant, says in Uzbek with a crowd of cheerful mixed voices in unison: "Joyimiz tor!" An off-screen narrator says in Uzbek with a warm storyteller's male voice: "Davomi — powerty.uz da." No subtitles, no on-screen text.
